name: Antu Danda (Shree Antu)
tagline: Sunrise ridge at 2,328 m on the Nepal–India border
meta_description: Antu Danda (Shree Antu) sunrise guide: 2,328 m view tower in Ilam, Kanchenjunga views, Lepcha villages, timing, how to reach from Fikkal and Ilam.
summary: Antu Danda, in Shree Antu village of Ilam district, is a 2,328 m ridge on the Nepal–India border famous for sunrise. On clear mornings the sun rises over the plains while Kanchenjunga turns pink in the north. It is about an hour's drive from Fikkal. Go between October and April and leave before 5 a.m.
intro: Shree Antu is a farming village in Suryodaya municipality whose hilltop, Antu Danda, is the best-known sunrise point in eastern Nepal. A view tower stands on the summit at 2,328 m, right on the border ridge that separates Ilam from the Darjeeling hills. The village around it grows tea, cardamom and garlic, and is home to a Lepcha community as well as Rai, Limbu and other hill families.

The draw is the morning show. The ridge faces east over the Terai and the plains of north Bengal, so on clear days the sun rises out of a flat horizon, often over a sea of cloud filling the valleys. Turn north and the Kanchenjunga range catches the first light. The best chances of a clear sky are from October to February; from March the haze thickens and by June the monsoon cloud usually hides everything.

Most visitors drive up in the dark from Fikkal, Kanyam or Ilam, watch the sunrise, then walk down to the small Antu Pokhari pond and the tea gardens before breakfast. Weekend mornings in season can be crowded with cars and day trippers from Jhapa and Siliguri. Homestays near the top let you skip the pre-dawn drive and walk up in 15 minutes.
facts: 50 min flight to Bhadrapur + 3 h drive
Sunrise, Kanchenjunga view, tea gardens, Lepcha community

highlights.title: Sunrise from the view tower
highlights.text: The tower on the 2,328 m summit gives a clear horizon to the east. Arrive 30 to 40 minutes before sunrise to watch the sky colour over the plains. In November that means being at the top by about 5.30 a.m.

highlights.title: Kanchenjunga at first light
highlights.text: Look north as the sun comes up. On clear winter mornings the Kanchenjunga massif, about 90 km away, turns pink then gold above the dark green hills of Ilam and Panchthar.

highlights.title: Cloud sea over the valleys
highlights.text: In autumn and winter, cold air often fills the valleys below with cloud, so the ridge stands above a white sea while the sun rises. It is the classic Antu Danda photograph.

highlights.title: Antu Pokhari and tea slopes
highlights.text: After sunrise, walk down to the small Antu Pokhari pond and the tea gardens around the village. The paths are short and easy, and tea stalls serve hot drinks to warm up.

highlights.title: Lepcha village life
highlights.text: Shree Antu is one of the few places in Nepal with a Lepcha community, a people more often associated with Sikkim and Darjeeling. Homestays here can introduce you to Lepcha food and traditions.

how_to_reach.text: From Fikkal it is ≈ 20 km and 45 minutes to 1 hour on a paved but narrow road. From Ilam Bazaar allow about 1.5–2 hours. From Kakarbhitta it is ≈ 80 km and about 3 hours, so most people stay overnight nearby.
Fly Kathmandu–Bhadrapur (50 min) and drive ≈ 85 km, about 3 hours, via Birtamod, Charali and Fikkal.
From homestays in Shree Antu village the walk to the view tower takes 15 to 30 minutes on a clear path. Bring a torch for the pre-dawn walk.

where_to_stay: Shree Antu village has a growing number of homestays and small lodges within walking distance of the view tower, which saves a 4 a.m. drive; rooms are simple, with shared or attached bathrooms and home-cooked meals. More choice is in Fikkal, about 45 minutes away, which has several hotels, and in Ilam Bazaar, about 1.5–2 hours away. In peak weekends of November and December, rooms near the top fill early. We confirm a recently checked property with your quote.
tips: Check sunrise time the night before and leave Fikkal at least 75 minutes earlier.
Wear a down jacket, hat and gloves: winter dawns on the ridge are often 0 to 5 °C with wind.
Weekday mornings are much quieter than Saturdays and public holidays.
If the summit is clouded in, wait 20 minutes; cloud often lifts briefly after sunrise.
Use the toilet before leaving your hotel; facilities at the top are basic.

experiences.title: Antu Danda sunrise trip from Fikkal
experiences.image_query: Antu Danda sunrise sea of clouds
experiences.summary: Drive from Fikkal in the dark to the 2,328 m view tower at Shree Antu, watch the sunrise over the plains and Kanchenjunga lighting up to the north, then walk the village tea slopes before breakfast.
body: Your driver collects you around 4.15 a.m. in November or December, a little later in late winter. The road climbs east from Fikkal through tea gardens and small villages to a parking area below the summit, about 45 minutes to an hour. From there it is a short walk to the view tower, where tea sellers are already setting up with flasks of hot milk tea.

The best colour comes in the 30 minutes before the sun appears. On a good morning the valleys below are filled with cloud, the plains of north Bengal stretch flat to the east and the sky turns orange, then gold. When the sun clears the horizon, turn north: the Kanchenjunga range, about 90 km away, glows pink. By March haze softens the view, and from June to September cloud usually hides it completely.

After sunrise we walk down to Antu Pokhari and through the tea gardens for 30 to 45 minutes, then drive back to Fikkal or Kanyam for breakfast. If your morning is cloudy, we try again the next day when the itinerary allows.

faqs.q: What time is sunrise at Antu Danda?
faqs.a: Roughly 5.30 a.m. in early November, around 6.15 a.m. in late December and January, and as early as 5 a.m. in May and June. Aim to reach the top 30 minutes before sunrise for the best colour.

faqs.q: Is Antu Danda worth it in the monsoon?
faqs.a: Usually not for views. From June to September the ridge is mostly in cloud and rain, and the narrow road can be slippery. The tea gardens are very green, but sunrise and mountain views are rare.

faqs.q: Can elderly people reach the view tower?
faqs.a: Yes. Cars park close to the top and the walk is short, though uneven and steep in places. Climbing the tower itself involves stairs; the view from the ground beside it is nearly as good.

experiences.title: Lepcha homestay night at Shree Antu
experiences.summary: Stay with a family in Shree Antu, one of the few Lepcha communities in Nepal, sharing an evening meal and stories of the village, then walk 15 minutes to the view tower for sunrise without the pre-dawn drive.
body: The Lepcha are an indigenous people of the Kanchenjunga foothills, best known in Sikkim and Darjeeling, with small communities on the Nepali side around Ilam. In Shree Antu a number of families, Lepcha and others, run homestays a short walk from the summit. Rooms are simple and clean, with thick quilts for winter nights, and meals are cooked in the family kitchen.

Dinner may include local greens, potatoes, homemade pickles, rice and, if you eat meat, chicken or pork, with millet or rice beer offered to those who want it. Hosts are usually happy to talk about their farming year, their language and their festivals, and in some houses you will see traditional bamboo and wooden crafts. The pace is slow and the evening ends early.

The reward comes at dawn: you walk up to the tower in 15 to 30 minutes by torchlight while others are still driving up from Fikkal. Not every homestay in Shree Antu is Lepcha-run, and we tell you honestly which family you are staying with.

faqs.a: The Lepcha are an indigenous people of the eastern Himalaya, centred on Sikkim and the Darjeeling hills, with a small community in Ilam district of Nepal. They have their own language and script and traditionally revere Kanchenjunga.

faqs.q: Are homestays at Shree Antu comfortable in winter?
faqs.a: They are simple but warm enough with heavy quilts. Nights from December to February can fall to around 0 °C, and rooms are rarely heated, so bring warm sleepwear and a hat.

faqs.q: Can we book a homestay near the view tower?
faqs.a: Yes. Several homestays sit within a 15 to 30 minute walk of the tower. Weekends in November and December fill early, so book at least two weeks ahead.

experiences.title: Ridge and tea-village walk down to Fikkal
experiences.summary: After sunrise, walk down from Shree Antu on village footpaths through tea gardens, cardamom gullies and small farms towards Fikkal, a gentle descent of about 800 m with the car following for anyone who wants to stop early.
body: This is a good choice for those who like to walk rather than ride. After sunrise and tea at the tower we follow footpaths and farm tracks downhill from Shree Antu, losing roughly 800 m over 12 to 14 km. The route cuts the corners of the road through tea gardens, past cardamom plots in shady gullies and through small hamlets where children walk to school and farmers carry leaf to collection points.

Our guide picks the best paths for the season and keeps the vehicle in touch by phone, so anyone can climb in after an hour or two. There are tea stops on the way and views across the Mechi valley to the Darjeeling ridge for most of the morning. The descent is easy on fitness but steady on the knees, so walking poles help.
We finish in Fikkal for a late lunch, in time to drive on to Ilam or down to Kakarbhitta in the afternoon. The walk is not marked, so go with a local guide rather than alone.

faqs.q: How difficult is the Antu Danda to Fikkal walk?
faqs.a: Easy to moderate. It is mostly downhill, about 800 m of descent over 12–14 km, on footpaths and farm tracks. Fitness matters less than good knees and shoes with grip.
Yes. The car follows on the road and meets us at several points, so you can walk for one or two hours and drive the rest.
We recommend one. Paths branch often through farms and are not signposted, and a local guide also makes conversations with villagers easier.

faqs.q: What is the height of Antu Danda?
faqs.a: The view tower on Antu Danda stands at 2,328 m above sea level, about 700 m higher than Kanyam and over 1,100 m higher than Ilam Bazaar. Altitude sickness is not a concern, but it is noticeably colder.

faqs.q: Can you see Everest from Antu Danda?
faqs.a: The main view is Kanchenjunga and its neighbours to the north. Some visitors report seeing distant peaks further west on exceptionally clear days, but you should go for Kanchenjunga and the sunrise, not Everest.

faqs.q: How far is Antu Danda from Siliguri?
faqs.a: About 115 km and 4 hours by road via the Kakarbhitta border, Charali and Fikkal, not counting time at the border. Most people sleep in Fikkal or Shree Antu and go up for sunrise.

faqs.q: What is the best month for Antu Danda?
faqs.a: November and December give the best mix of clear skies, cloud seas in the valleys and manageable cold. October, January and February are also good. Avoid June to September, when monsoon cloud usually covers the ridge.

faqs.q: Is there a fee at Antu Danda?
faqs.a: Small local fees for parking or climbing the view tower have been charged at times. Rules change, so check current status before you travel and carry some Nepali rupees.

faqs.q: Is Antu Danda the same as Shree Antu?
faqs.a: Yes, in practice. Shree Antu is the village and ward; Antu Danda, meaning Antu hill, is the summit with the view tower. Signs and maps use both names.

faqs.q: Can we go to Darjeeling from Antu Danda?
faqs.a: Not directly. The ridge is the border, and there is no official tourist crossing there. To reach Darjeeling you go down to Kakarbhitta, cross to Panitanki and drive up via Siliguri, about 5–6 hours.

faqs.q: Is Antu Danda good for kids?
faqs.a: Yes, if they can handle an early start. The walk from the car is short. Dress children warmly for the cold dawn and plan a nap later in the day.

faqs.q: Should I stay in Ilam or Fikkal for Antu Danda?
faqs.a: Fikkal or Shree Antu. From Fikkal the drive is under an hour; from Ilam Bazaar it is closer to 2 hours each way, meaning a 3.30 a.m. start in autumn.
